blocking.issue: Regression from the revision. The new push-path sentence says `ruralz bundle push` hands a Revision to Ruralz Control. 02-configuration-model.md forbids this: Ruralz Control never accepts a pre-rendered Revision. It takes the source Bundle and the digest the CLI computed, re-renders the Bundle with the Environment's variables, and rejects a mismatch with RZ-CFG-027. Only the OCI registry receives a rendered Revision.
blocking.evidence: Line 93: "`ruralz bundle push` can also hand a Revision to Ruralz Control or an OCI registry, from which file-mode Nodes pull Revisions and Plugin artifacts by digest." 02-configuration-model.md (Environment substitution): "Ruralz Control never accepts a pre-rendered Revision: `ruralz bundle push --env prod` to Ruralz Control uploads the source Bundle with the digest the CLI computed; Ruralz Control re-renders it ... rejects a mismatch with RZ-CFG-027 ... Pushing to an OCI registry uploads the rendered Revision for file-mode Nodes."
blocking.fix: Replace the sentence with: "`ruralz bundle push` can also upload a source Bundle to Ruralz Control, which re-renders it and checks the CLI's digest, or publish a rendered Revision to an OCI registry, from which file-mode Nodes pull Revisions and Plugin artifacts by digest." If Figure 1 gets a CLI-to-Control push edge, label it the same way.

blocking.issue: File mode lifecycle says the Node substitutes `${VAR}` while it reads `ruralz bundle render` output. In the configuration model, render output is already substituted: substitution runs once, after overlay merge, and a literal `${` is escaped as `$${`. File-mode `ruralzd` substitutes from its process environment only when it loads an unrendered source Bundle. The sentence also contradicts the Configuration lifecycle rule that the digest covers the render after substitution, because a Node that substitutes again could compute a different digest. The Source cell ('Rendered Bundle directory') is also narrower than the configuration model, which allows an unrendered source Bundle with no overlay. For a Cluster with more than one Node it only says rendered Bundles SHOULD be used.
blocking.evidence: Line 395: "The directory form reads `ruralz bundle render` output, since file-mode `ruralzd` applies no overlay; the Node substitutes `${VAR}` from its environment and computes the digest." Line 384: "Rendered Bundle directory at `RURALZ_CONFIG`, or a Revision pulled from OCI". 02-configuration-model.md: "| `ruralzd` in file mode | Its process environment, only when it loads an unrendered source Bundle |" and "A file-mode Cluster with more than one Node SHOULD load rendered Bundles or OCI Revisions".
blocking.fix: Line 395: "The directory form SHOULD hold `ruralz bundle render --env <env>` output, since file-mode `ruralzd` applies no overlay. Only when it loads an unrendered source Bundle does the Node substitute `${VAR}` from its process environment. Either way it computes the digest of what it loaded." Line 384 Source cell: "Bundle directory at `RURALZ_CONFIG` (rendered SHOULD be used for more than one Node), or a Revision pulled from OCI".

non_blocking.suggestion: The harness passed an empty prior-blocking list, but the previous on-disk L2 verdict listed L2-1 to L2-6. All six are resolved: the onRoute work now matches the Policy registry; OQ-14 is resolved and the digest sentence matches the configuration model; OQ-4 and OQ-5 are removed and the Plugin trap row cites `failureMode` default `closed`; `spec.rollout` strategy and `autoRollback` are honored and batch sizing is in OQ-17; TB-7 no longer implies `secretRef`; the milestone cells are split. The new findings are numbered from L2-7 to avoid ID collisions.

Line 56 and Figure 2 add a second control-plane persistence area, 'Revision content by digest ... (a replicated blob directory or the OCI registry)' plus 'audit segments', outside the Control Store. The foundation pack names exactly one control-plane persistence, the Control Store, and the architecture summary says Ruralz Control 'keeps its operational state in a Raft-replicated Control Store'. Either describe the blob area as part of the Control Store (for example 'Control Store content area, stored by digest outside the Raft log') or add an OQ or foundation amendment for the new storage tier.

Figure 3's opt block 'Rate Limit or Quota Policy attached' applies the local token bucket and GCRA EVAL to Quotas. ADR-0008 covers Rate Limits only, and the configuration model says `quota` 'checks in `onRequestHeaders` and increments at `onLog`'. Label the opt 'Rate Limit Policy attached' and add a separate note: 'Quota: one check, settled in onLog'.

Line 248: 'a per-Node ceiling declared on the Policy (field owned by Traffic management and resilience, OQ-configuration-model-9)'. OQ-configuration-model-9 asks who authors config schemas, not whether this field exists, and the `ratelimit` fixed fields are only `key` and `limits[]`. Add a dedicated OQ (for example OQ-system-overview-21: 'How is the per-Node ceiling for `ratelimit` declared?'), as the style guide requires for fields not yet in the configuration model.

Line 270 states as design that the Token Budget 'counts locally in `onChunk` from streamed usage deltas or an estimate and ends the stream'. ADR-0014 limits the tokenizer to pre-admission estimates, and the document itself makes this OQ-system-overview-20 (blocking). Make the sentence conditional: 'ends the stream from streamed usage deltas; estimate-based enforcement awaits OQ-system-overview-20'.

The `/readyz` definition (line 372) and Figure 5 'Last-Known-Good loaded' omit a condition from the configuration model: a Node cold-starting from Last-Known-Good fails `/readyz` until every `secretRef` resolves. Append 'with every `secretRef` resolved' to the `/readyz` rule.

Line 427, 'Both are Planned (M1)', follows definitions of three terms (Hot Reload, Rollout, Zero-Downtime Upgrade), and Rollout is Planned (M2). Write 'Hot Reload and Zero-Downtime Upgrade are Planned (M1)'.

Line 399, 'a Node warns when its Cluster reports more than one Node', assumes Control mode, where the Node count is known. The configuration model's rule is a startup warning whenever the `memory` driver is used. Align the wording, or say the Cluster-count warning is in addition to the startup warning.
Carried over: the rules table still does not name the P-ID each rule derives from. Add a 'Principle' column (for example P10 for 'Degraded states are observable').
Word count is about 3,987 under word_count_rule, only 13 below the 4,000 cap. Any fix above that adds words should be offset by a cut, for example by shortening the Reconnect behavior paragraph.

foundation_amendments: Section 2 (Canonical names), Last-Known-Good row: distinguish the 'active Revision' (what a Node serves, including while detached from Ruralz Control) from Last-Known-Good (the persisted boot Revision, promoted at the Cluster's promoted digest in Control mode).
